_comment: Supplemental curated orthography profiles (agent-curated, 2026 audit). Keyed by ISO 639-3. Each entry has: 'ortho' — a phoneme -> grapheme map in the ORTHO format ('/'-separated alternatives), keys chosen from the language's PHOIBLE-attested chart symbols plus canonical non-chart phonemes; and 'profile' — a full per-letter row set in the VERIFIED_LANGUAGE_PROFILES shape. Consumed by scripts/build_data.py, emitted into data.js as SUPPLEMENTAL_ORTHO / SUPPLEMENTAL_LANGUAGE_PROFILES, merged at runtime in app-core.js (baseline data always wins). Doculect artifacts with no orthographic basis are deliberately left unmapped so they stay blue. 'status' values must exist in verificationLabel() in app-core.js.

profile.title: Classical Latin alphabet (late Republic)
profile.variety: Latin of the late Roman Republic (c. 100–27 BC), reconstructed pronunciation
profile.completeness: All 23 letters of the classical alphabet are represented; J, U and W are later medieval distinctions.
profile.notes: Historical reconstruction — this language is outside the PHOIBLE dataset and never enters L or P. Vowel letters each cover a short/long pair (a/ā, e/ē…); I and V double as the glides /j w/. Reconstruction follows W. S. Allen, Vox Latina.

sources.title: W. S. Allen, Vox Latina: The Pronunciation of Classical Latin (2nd ed., CUP)

rows.note: Always /k/; archaic /ɡ/ survives in the abbreviations C. and Cn.
Also the first element of GN [ŋn] (agnus).
Weak; often dropped in popular speech.
Short [ɪ], long [iː]; consonantal /j/ before a vowel (no separate J).
Archaic; fixed forms such as Kalendae.
Word-final -M largely nasalized the preceding vowel.
Short [ʊ], long [uː]; consonantal /w/ before a vowel (no separate U/W).
Greek loans; reintroduced in the 1st century BC.

profile.title: Malayalam alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant and vowel letters of modern Malayalam are represented.
profile.notes: Malayalam distinguishes two rhotics (ര/റ) and the retroflex continuant ഴ. Aspirated letters occur mainly in Sanskrit loans. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Odia alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant and vowel letters of modern Odia are represented.
profile.notes: The inherent vowel of Odia is /ɔ/, not /ə/. Aspirated letters occur throughout. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Hokkien (Pe̍h-ōe-jī romanization)
profile.completeness: All Pe̍h-ōe-jī initials and vowel letters are represented.
profile.notes: Hokkien is written with Chinese characters in everyday use; characters map to syllables, not phonemes. This profile uses the Pe̍h-ōe-jī (POJ) romanization, following the Mandarin/Pinyin precedent. Final -h marks the glottal-stop coda; o͘ (o with dot) is /ɔ/. Agent-curated.

rows.note: Initial /h/; final -h spells the glottal stop.

profile.title: Nigerian Pidgin orthography
profile.completeness: The practical Latin orthography in common written use is represented.
profile.notes: Spelling is not fully standardized; the widely used practical orthography does not distinguish /e/–/ɛ/ or /o/–/ɔ/, both written e and o. Labio-velars kp/gb occur in loanwords from Nigerian languages. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Hakka (Pha̍k-fa-sṳ romanization)
profile.completeness: All Pha̍k-fa-sṳ initials and principal vowel letters are represented.
profile.notes: Hakka is written with Chinese characters in everyday use; characters map to syllables, not phonemes. This profile uses the Pha̍k-fa-sṳ (PFS) romanization, following the Mandarin/Pinyin precedent. [ç] is the palatalized h (hi-); [ɲ] the palatalized ng (ngi-). Agent-curated.

profile.title: Malay orthography (Rumi)
profile.completeness: The complete modern Rumi orthography is represented; the Jawi (Arabic) script is not covered by this profile.
profile.notes: The letter e covers both /ə/ and /e/. Word-final k commonly spells the glottal stop. f, v, z, sy, kh occur in loanwords. Agent-curated from the joint Malaysian–Indonesian spelling conventions.

profile.title: Hausa Boko alphabet
profile.completeness: The complete official Boko orthography is represented, including the hooked letters ɓ ɗ ƙ and the digraphs sh, ts.
profile.notes: Hausa's two rhotics (tap and retroflex flap) are both written r. Vowel length and tone are not marked in standard orthography. The Ajami (Arabic) script is not covered. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Bhojpuri Devanagari alphabet
profile.completeness: The Devanagari letters in Bhojpuri use are represented; the historical Kaithi script is not covered.
profile.notes: Follows Hindi Devanagari conventions; the inherent vowel is transcribed /ʌ~ə/. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Sundanese Latin orthography
profile.completeness: The complete modern Latin orthography is represented; the traditional Aksara Sunda script is not covered.
profile.notes: The digraph eu spells the distinctive central vowel /ɨ/; e is schwa and é is /ɛ~e/. Word-final k commonly spells the glottal stop. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Moroccan Arabic (Darija) orthography
profile.completeness: The Arabic-script letters in common Darija use are represented, including the Maghrebi gāf ݣ.
profile.notes: Darija spelling is not fully standardized; Arabic-script conventions are given. ج is /ʒ/ in Moroccan Arabic; ق varies between /q/ and /ɡ/ by word and region. Short vowels are normally unwritten. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Uzbek Latin alphabet
profile.completeness: The complete official Latin alphabet is represented, including oʻ, gʻ, sh, ch, ng.
profile.notes: Uzbek o spells the back rounded /ɒ/ and a the fronted /æ~a/; oʻ is /ɵ~oː/ and u is /u~ʉ/. The Cyrillic orthography remains in parallel use and is not covered. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Awadhi Devanagari alphabet
profile.completeness: The Devanagari letters in Awadhi use are represented; the historical Kaithi script is not covered.
profile.notes: Follows Hindi Devanagari conventions. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Cebuano alphabet
profile.completeness: The practical Latin orthography in common use is represented.
profile.notes: Cebuano has a three-vowel core /a i u/ with [o u] and [e i] alternating; o and e appear in spelling for the lower variants. The glottal stop is written with a hyphen word-internally and unmarked finally. Agent-curated.

rows.note: Hyphen spells the word-internal glottal stop.

profile.title: Yoruba alphabet
profile.completeness: The complete standard orthography is represented, including the subdot letters ẹ ọ ṣ and the digraph gb.
profile.notes: The letter p spells the labio-velar /k͡p/ (plain [p] does not occur natively); gb is its voiced counterpart /ɡ͡b/. Tone is marked with accents in careful writing. Nasal vowels are spelled with a following n. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Igbo alphabet (Ọnwụ)
profile.completeness: The complete Ọnwụ orthography is represented, including ị ọ ụ ṅ and the digraphs ch gb gh gw kp kw nw ny sh.
profile.notes: Igbo has vowel harmony across the two vowel sets (i e u o vs. ị a ụ ọ). kp and gb are labio-velar stops. Tone is not normally marked. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Sudanese Arabic orthography
profile.completeness: The Arabic-script letters in Sudanese use are represented.
profile.notes: In Sudanese Arabic ق is realized /ɡ/ and ج is [ɡʲ~ɟ]; the interdental letters merge with stops or sibilants. Short vowels are normally unwritten. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Saraiki alphabet
profile.completeness: The Urdu-based letter set plus the four Saraiki implosive letters ٻ ڄ ݙ ڳ and retroflex ݨ are represented.
profile.notes: Saraiki is distinctive for its four implosives, each with a dedicated letter. Arabic-origin letters merge as in Urdu. Short vowels are diacritics and normally unwritten. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Malagasy orthography
profile.completeness: The complete standard orthography is represented.
profile.notes: Distinctive values: the letter o spells /u/ (ô is /o/ in loans), j spells /dz/, and y is the word-final form of /i/. The affricates ts/tr and j/dr contrast. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Nepali Devanagari alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant and vowel letters of Nepali Devanagari are represented.
profile.notes: Follows standard Devanagari conventions; the inherent vowel is transcribed /ʌ~ə/. च/ज are affricates [ts~tʃ]/[dz~dʒ]. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Fulfulde (Nigeria) alphabet
profile.completeness: The standard Latin orthography is represented, including the hooked letters ɓ ɗ ƴ and the velar nasal ŋ.
profile.notes: The five vowel letters cover the tense/lax pairs. ƴ spells the glottalized palatal glide. The Adlam script and Ajami are not covered by this profile. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Maithili Devanagari alphabet
profile.completeness: The Devanagari letters in Maithili use are represented; the historical Tirhuta (Mithilakshar) script is not covered.
profile.notes: Follows standard Devanagari conventions. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Assamese alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary letters are represented, including the distinctively Assamese ৰ (ra) and ৱ (wa).
profile.notes: Assamese is notable for spirantized values: চ/ছ are /s/, জ/য are /z/, and শ/ষ/স all spell the velar fricative /x/. The inherent vowel is /ɔ~o/. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Madurese Latin orthography
profile.completeness: The modern Latin orthography is represented; the traditional Carakan script is not covered.
profile.notes: Retroflexes are written th/dh following the Javanese convention; â spells the distinctive back unrounded vowel /ɤ/. Word-final k commonly spells the glottal stop. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Isan (Northeastern Thai) in Thai script
profile.completeness: The Thai-script letters used for writing Isan are represented; the historical Tai Noi script is not covered.
profile.notes: Isan is written in the Thai script in Thailand. Distinctively Lao features carry over: ย commonly spells /ɲ/ where Thai has /j/, and ว is /v~w/. Tone values differ from Central Thai. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Urdu alphabet
profile.completeness: All base letters of the Urdu alphabet are represented; aspirated series are written with the following do-chashmi he (ھ).
profile.notes: Multiple letters of Arabic origin merge to single Urdu phonemes (e.g. س/ص/ث → /s/, ز/ض/ذ/ظ → /z/). Short vowels are diacritics (zabar/zer/pesh) and are normally unwritten. Agent-curated from standard descriptions; broad phonemic values.

rows.note: Etymological Arabic ʿayn; typically vocalic or silent in Urdu.
rows.name: 'ain

rows.note: Nūn ghunna: nasalizes the preceding vowel.
rows.name: nūn ghunna

profile.title: Punjabi Gurmukhi alphabet
profile.completeness: All 35 base letters plus the six bindi (dotted) letters are represented.
profile.notes: Tonal contrasts derive historically from the voiced-aspirate letters (ਘ ਝ ਢ ਧ ਭ) and ਹ; tones themselves are not written. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Telugu alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant letters and vowel letters of modern Telugu are represented.
profile.notes: Aspirated consonant letters occur mainly in Sanskrit loans. Short/long vowel pairs share a base letter shape. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

rows.note: Palatal affricate; [ts] before back vowels in native words.
[dz] before back vowels in native words.

profile.title: Marathi Devanagari (Balbodh) alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant and vowel letters of Marathi Balbodh are represented, including ळ and the loan-vowel signs ॲ/ऑ.
profile.notes: Marathi additionally distinguishes the affricate values of च/ज ([ts/tʃ], [dz/dʒ]) by following vowel; broad values are given. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Javanese Latin orthography
profile.completeness: The complete modern Latin orthography is represented; the traditional Aksara Jawa script is not covered by this profile.
profile.notes: Retroflex stops are written th/dh. Word-final k commonly spells the glottal stop [ʔ]. The letters é/è disambiguate /e/ and /ɛ/ from schwa e in careful writing. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Shanghainese Wu (Wugniu romanization)
profile.completeness: Initials and principal vowel letters of the Wugniu scheme are represented.
profile.notes: Wu is written with Chinese characters in everyday use; characters map to syllables, not phonemes. This profile uses the Wugniu romanization as the phoneme-addressable orthography, following the Mandarin/Pinyin precedent. Final -q marks the glottal-stop coda; gh marks the voiced/breathy onset. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Cantonese (Jyutping romanization)
profile.completeness: All Jyutping initials and vowel nuclei are represented.
profile.notes: Cantonese is written with Chinese characters in everyday use; characters map to syllables, not phonemes. This profile uses the LSHK Jyutping romanization as the phoneme-addressable orthography, following the Mandarin/Pinyin precedent. Paired spellings b/p, d/t, g/k, z/c encode the unaspirated/aspirated contrast. Agent-curated.

profile.title: Filipino alphabet
profile.completeness: All 28 letters of the modern Filipino alphabet are represented.
profile.notes: The glottal stop is phonemic but has no letter; word-internally it is written with a hyphen (pag-asa) and finally it is unmarked. The letters c, ñ, q, v, x, z occur in proper names and unassimilated loans. Agent-curated from the KWF orthography.

rows.note: Hyphen spells the word-internal glottal stop (pag-asa); final ʔ is unmarked.

profile.title: Gujarati alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant and vowel letters of modern Gujarati are represented, including the loan-vowel signs ઍ/ઑ.
profile.notes: Aspirated letters occur throughout the native vocabulary. Murmured vowels and the ə/a distinction follow standard descriptions. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Thai script
profile.completeness: All 44 consonant letters and the principal vowel signs are represented.
profile.notes: Many letters share a phoneme and differ only in tone class and etymology (e.g. ข ฃ ค ฅ ฆ all /kʰ/). Consonant values differ syllable-finally (e.g. ล → [n]). Vowels are written with signs around the consonant; tones are marked separately. Agent-curated after Tingsabadh & Abramson (1993).

rows.note: Also silent tone marker before sonorants.
rows.name: ho hip

profile.title: Kannada alphabet
profile.completeness: All primary consonant and vowel letters of modern Kannada are represented.
profile.notes: Aspirated letters occur mainly in Sanskrit loans. Short/long vowel pairs share a base letter shape. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

profile.title: Pashto alphabet
profile.completeness: All Pashto letters including the retroflex series (ټ ډ ړ ڼ) and the dialect letters ښ/ږ are represented.
profile.notes: The letters ښ and ږ vary by dialect: [ç/x] and [ʝ/ɡ] in the north, [ʂ] and [ʐ] in the south — both values are mapped. Arabic-origin letters merge as in Urdu. Agent-curated; broad phonemic values.

rows.note: Etymological Arabic ʿayn; typically vocalic or silent.
rows.name: ayn
